amendments.rule: Where a textual unit's decision leaves the projection carrying a reading the ASV **excludes**, English that answers to the missing source word is `added` under rule 5, and the note must carry enough for a later reader to check it: the unit id, the reading the projection carries, the readings that remained, and why the word is absent. Rule 12 is untouched — this is the citation, not a second vote on the unit. Two kinds of decision do it and the packet signals only the first. It marks an **underdetermined** unit whose fallback the evidence ruled out `FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE` beneath its variant line, and an underdetermined unit whose fallback is still among the readings the English permits carries no such mark and is not this case; but a **selected** unit carries no mark either, and where the reading it selects is shorter than the one the ASV translated the English is `added` on exactly the same terms, the note naming the selected reading in place of the excluded fallback. So the absence of the mark settles nothing on its own: read the variant line. `ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ` → *by Christ Jesus* at PHP.3.12 leaves *Jesus* `added`, `SBLGNT.PHP.3.12.v007` having kept r01 `Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ` and r02 `τοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ` while the projection carries the bare base the English rules out; the verse-opening *And* of JHN.9.28 is `added` for the same reason, `SBLGNT.JHN.9.28.v029` having kept the connectives of r01 `καὶ` and r02 `οἱ δὲ` against an asyndetic base; and *kneeling down* at MRK.1.40 is `added` on the selected arm, `SBLGNT.MRK.1.40.v057` having selected r02, which carries no participle of kneeling though the ASV translates one. JHN.10.13 is the same shape for a whole clause and is the standard for the note. A textual note the ASV prints of its own — *Some ancient authorities omit the Son of God* at MRK.1.1, *Some ancient authorities omit and kneeling down to him* at MRK.1.40 — corroborates the reading and belongs in the note, but it does not license the status by itself: what licenses it is that no token of the projection answers to the English. Rule 37 is the near contrast and is worth ruling out by name, because the two look alike from the English side: there the licensing token stands in a neighbouring verse, here it stands in no verse of the projection at all. Do not reach for rule 7 to fold such a word onto a neighbouring token — a helper belongs to the word that licenses it, and the word that would have licensed this one is absent — and do not reach for `noncompositional`. Rule 11 does not decide this either way, the ASV italicizing such a word only sometimes. The mirror case, where the projection carries an excluded reading **longer** than the ASV's, makes the surplus tokens their own `unrepresented` unit and owes the same note; no corpus unit has needed it yet.
amendments.why: MRK.1.40's *kneeling down* is `added` because the unit's **selected** reading r02 carries no participle of kneeling, while the ASV translates one. Rule 97's opening sentence already covers this — the decision leaves the projection carrying a reading the ASV excludes — but its next sentence, 'You are told when it has happened', describes only the `FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE` mark, which a selected unit never carries. Read as it stood, that sentence tells a verse pass the case does not arise, and the pass has to reason around the rule instead of from it. The amendment names the second arm, keeps the underdetermined-fallback exclusion exactly as it was, and adds the standard for citing an ASV margin note, which corroborated both of this chapter's textual `added` units without being what licensed either. Nothing in the corpus contradicts it: rule 97's own two examples are the fallback arm and are preserved verbatim.

amendments.rule: An English particle or adverb that realizes a Greek **preverb** rides inside the compound verb's own unit and is never `added`, as a discontinuous realization under rule 15 where the ASV separates them: `ἐξῆλθεν` → *went forth*, `ἐξέβαλον` → *cast out*, `ἀνέβη` → *went up*, `ἐπεβίβασαν` → *set thereon* at LUK.19.35, `προσηργάσατο` → *hath made more* at LUK.19.16, `ἀπολάβωσιν` → *receive again* at LUK.6.34. The head is the English word glossing the **verbal root**, never the particle. The corpus is unanimous: 963 units across 141 chapters carry such a particle and every one of them is `aligned`, none `added`, and the head stands on the verb word in all but one class. This is scoped to a particle **no Greek preposition stands to answer to**. Where an expressed preposition does answer to it — because the particle is part of that preposition's own English gloss, as *out* is of `ἐκ` → *out of* — the whole English prepositional expression is the preposition's, headed on the prepositional word, and the compound verb keeps only its verb word: `ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ` → *come* and *out of*, `ἐξῆλθεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ` → *came* and *out of*, as `εἰσελθὼν εἰς` → *entered* and *into* and `ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ` → *departed* and *from* do. Rule 36 is what decides that and says it in terms: an English preposition governing a prepositional phrase realizes the Greek preposition and not the verb it depends on, even where English idiom makes the verb phrasal, and a preposition is left `unrepresented` only where English realizes it nowhere at all — so do not leave such a preposition a bare *of* while the verb takes the *out*. A preverb whose sense the following preposition's gloss does **not** carry keeps this rule's ordinary treatment, which is why `ἀναβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος` → *coming up out of the water* gives *up* to the participle and *out of* to `ἐκ` in one clause, and why `ἐκβάλλει … εἰς` → *driveth … forth* and *into* does. Rule 94 decides only whether the preposition and the word it governs form one unit, and does not decide where the particle goes. Where the compound verb governs a bare dative or genitive that the ASV writes with an English preposition, that preposition realizes the case government and rides with the governed word under rules 21, 36 and 69, as MRK.14.65 has it. The one exception is an idiom that leaves no English verb word to head on at all: `Ἆρον` → *away with him* at JHN.19.15 and `Αἶρε` → *away with* at LUK.23.18 head on *away*, because nothing else was written.
amendments.why: MRK.1 has seven verses in which a compound verb stands next to an expressed cognate preposition, and rule 106's scope clause sent the verse pass to rule 94, which answers a different question — whether a preposition merges with the word it governs — and says nothing about where the particle goes. Two verses (1:25, 1:26) had to be corrected mid-pass for that reason. The amendment keeps every sentence of rule 106 intact and replaces the dangling pointer with the answer rule 36 already gives, plus the test that separates the two cases: whether the particle is part of the preposition's own gloss. 1:10 is the control and settles the test from inside one clause, giving *up* to ἀναβαίνων and *out of* to ἐκ. Nothing in the corpus is contradicted — rule 106's 963-unit count is for the case where no preposition stands, which the rule's own scope clause already excluded, and rule 36's `περιεζωσμένοι … περὶ τὰ στήθη` → *girt about their breasts* is the same shape decided the same way.

conventions: Where a compound verb's preverb is echoed by an expressed cognate preposition, the whole English prepositional expression belongs to the preposition, headed on the prepositional word, and the verb keeps only its verb word: `ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ` → *come* and *out of* (1:25), `ἐξῆλθεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ` → *came* and *out of* (1:26), `ἐξελθόντες ἐκ` → *when they were come* and *out of* (1:29), `εἰσελθὼν εἰς` → *entered* and *into* (1:21, 1:45), `ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ` → *departed* and *from* (1:42). Where the preverb is not part of the following preposition's own gloss the particle stays inside the verb's unit under rule 106, which is why 1:10 gives *up* to ἀναβαίνων and *out of* to ἐκ in one clause, and 1:12 gives *forth* to ἐκβάλλει and *into* to εἰς. 1:5, 1:28, 1:34, 1:35, 1:38, 1:39, 1:43 and 1:45 keep the particle on the verb because no preposition stands there at all.

A periphrastic ἦν + participle keeps the finite copula's own English on ἦν and the lexical verb word on the participle: *was* at 1:6 (*was clothed*) and 1:33 (*was gathered together*), and the supplied subject *he* at 1:22, where the ASV collapses the periphrasis into the simple past *he taught*. The differing surface is the ASV's, not two analyses (rule 24). Do not read the collapse as leaving ἦν `unrepresented`, and do not give the supplied subject to the participle.

Where a denominative Greek verb is rendered by a generic English verb plus the noun of its own root, the head is that noun: `σπλαγχνισθείς` → *being moved with compassion* on *compassion* (1:41), `πυρέσσουσα` → *sick of a fever* on *fever* (1:30), `δαιμονιζομένους` → *that were possessed with demons* on *demons* (1:32). Where the root is itself verbal the head is the verb word, as `ἀμφιβάλλοντας` → *casting a net* on *casting* (1:16), `ἐμβριμησάμενος` → *he strictly charged* on *charged* (1:43) and `ἐπισυνηγμένη` → *gathered together* on *gathered* (1:33) do. `ἤγγικεν` → *is at hand* on *hand* (1:15) is not an exception but rule 71's recorded corpus reading of the ἐγγ- family.

Two of the chapter's three `added` units rest on textual decisions rather than on rule 86, and a later reader should not read them as ordinary supplied English. *the Son of God* at 1:1 is rule 97's fallback case, SBLGNT.MRK.1.1.v001 being marked FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE with r01 and r02 carrying υἱοῦ θεοῦ. *kneeling down* at 1:40 is the selected-reading case, SBLGNT.MRK.1.40.v057 having selected r02, which carries no participle of kneeling though the ASV translates one; the packet marks such a unit in no way at all. The ASV's own margin corroborates both but licenses neither by itself. Only 1:9's *that* is rule 86's case: a finite indicative the ASV subordinates with no conjunction anywhere in the verse.

report: Read all 54 candidate groups and then the full dump end to end, since the table is keyed by source lemma and is blind to `added` units, which is where the drift I was hunting lives.

SPLIT FOUND AND FIXED. One construction — a denominative Greek verb rendered by a generic English verb plus the noun of its own root — was headed two ways. 1:41 `σπλαγχνισθείς` → *being moved with compassion* heads on *compassion*, and 1:30 `πυρέσσουσα` → *sick of a fever* heads on *fever*, its note reasoning from `πυρετός` → *fever* in the next verse; but 1:32 `δαιμονιζομένους` → *that were possessed with demons* heads on *possessed* and its note calls *with demons* a supplied completion — the opposite reasoning for the same shape, with nothing in the source licensing the difference. Resolved toward the root-bearing noun: rules 17, 66 and 91 and rule 104's root-family query all point there, and `δαιμόνιον` → *demons* stands twice in this chapter (1:34, 1:39). The alternative would have meant patching 1:41 and 1:30 against the contract instead. Only the target head of MRK.1.32 s017 moves, t021 → t023; unit membership is untouched.

Preverb versus expressed preposition: the chapter is consistent, and what was wrong is the contract. 1:25 and 1:26 were corrected in the verse pass to give *out of* whole to `ἐξ`, the compound verb keeping a bare *come* / *came*; 1:10, 1:11 and 1:29 already read that way, and 1:21, 1:42 and 1:45 do the same for `εἰς` and `ἀπό`. 1:10 writes both halves in one clause — *up* inside `ἀναβαίνων`'s unit, *out of* on `ἐκ` — which shows the test is whether the particle is part of the preposition's own gloss. Rule 106 scopes itself away from this case and points at rule 94, but rule 94 decides only whether a preposition merges with the word it governs and never says where the particle goes. Amended 106 to point at rule 36, which answers it in terms.

Periphrastic `ἦν` + participle is one analysis across 1:6, 1:22 and 1:33: the finite copula keeps its own English — *was* at 1:6 and 1:33, the supplied subject *he* at 1:22 where the ASV collapses the periphrasis into a simple past — and the participle keeps the lexical verb word. Recorded as a convention, since the surface differs and the token could easily drift to `unrepresented`.

Articles: every one of the 44 `unrepresented` units traces to rule 20 displacement (by a genitive pronoun at 1:2, 1:3, 1:5, 1:6, 1:7, 1:11, 1:19, 1:20, 1:22, 1:23, 1:39, 1:41, 1:44; by an English *'s* at 1:30), to rule 23 (before a name, before a place name, a second attributive article, or a determinerless noun), to rule 38 at 1:9, or to rule 61 at 1:14. None is emptied for convenience, and no article carries a bare *of* or *unto*.

The `added` audit is clean. Three units only: 1:9 *that* under rule 86 (finite indicative, no conjunction anywhere to realize), 1:1 *the Son of God* under rule 97's fallback case, and 1:40 *kneeling down* under a selected reading. Every other supplied English word is folded onto a licensing token, and consistently so — determiners on the noun (rules 51, 58) at 1:1, 1:3, 1:4, 1:6, 1:8, 1:10, 1:11, 1:23, 1:26, 1:27, 1:35, 1:44, 1:45; copulas on the predicate (rule 53) at 1:7, 1:19, 1:32, 1:34, 1:36; subjects and expletives on the verb (rule 9) throughout; junctures on the verb they introduce (rule 88) at 1:18, 1:20, 1:21, 1:31 twice, 1:35, 1:41, 1:43, 1:45; and supplied objects and complements on the verb that requires them (rules 7, 74) at 1:16, 1:31, 1:32, 1:41, 1:45.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error, and I changed no accepted edge. MRK.1.4 `ὁ` is rule 31 — the name `Ἰωάννης` is the expressed head noun, and rule 90 says in terms that it blesses no unit where one is. MRK.1.7 `τῶν` and MRK.1.23 `τῇ` are rule 20 displacement, by *whose* and by *their*. MRK.1.14 `τό` is the nominalizing article of an articular infinitive, which rule 61 empties by name. MRK.1.32 `γενομένης` has no English of its own once the ASV compresses `Ὀψίας γενομένης` into *at even*, and *at* is the case preposition riding with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause.

Residual judgments I left standing, each already carrying its own note, so a later reader can act on them without re-deriving the question: 1:20 `μισθωτῶν` headed on *hired* rather than *servants* (rule 66's `πλεονέκτης` → *covetous man* is the direct analogue); 1:35 the division of *a great while before day* between `ἔννυχα` and `λίαν`; 1:7 the single *whose* given to `οὗ` with the resumptive `αὐτοῦ` left empty; 1:45 `πάντοθεν` → *from every quarter* headed on *quarter*, which follows the chapter's own uniform treatment of adverbs rendered by phrases (1:35 three times) and rule 71's frame precedent, against a reading that would head the quantifier word.

No corpus request. The two head questions I could not settle from the packet — `δαιμονίζομαι` and `ἐκ` → *out of* — are both decided by contract rules already in force (91 and 104 for the first, 36 for the second), and neither would change a patch: the chapter is internally consistent on `ἐκ` either way, and the `δαιμονίζομαι` split has to be resolved one way or the other regardless of what a query would return.
